    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Watchdog enable configuration",
      "Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Information": "The run-time setting that enables watchdog counting and timeout processing; watchdog operation depends on retaining the intended enable state.",

        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"

      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker who changes the watchdog enable through a bus write could disable timeout protection or unexpectedly activate it.",

        "bus_req_i.data"

      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity: the lock is stored and changed from bus data at lines 76 and 95, and it controls subsequent configuration writes at line 93. Availability: the lock can block bus writes to the watchdog configuration at lines 93-100.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could alter or force the lock state so that malicious configuration is accepted or required watchdog updates are refused.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],

      "Information": "The stored limit against which watchdog elapsed time is compared; watchdog protection depends on this setting to determine when a timeout reset occurs.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity: a bus write stores the timeout limit at line 97 and a changed limit alters the comparison at line 144. Availability: the comparison drives timeout reset generation at lines 155 and 161, so a modified limit can suppress or prematurely trigger reset.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could write an excessive or very small timeout limit to prevent recovery resets or cause repeated unexpected resets.",

        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],

    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Watchdog elapsed-time state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Information": "The internally held elapsed-count and started state used to track watchdog progress; it has no entry or exit port because it is maintained internally and only contributes to the timeout decision.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity: the elapsed count and started state are held and updated at lines 126-134, so corrupting them changes watchdog progress. Availability: the state determines the timeout condition at line 144 and therefore whether reset generation occurs at lines 155-161.",

        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could corrupt the elapsed state to keep the watchdog from expiring or to force an early reset.",

      "Concept Name": "Watchdog-generated system reset control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Information": "The reset assertion generated from watchdog timeout or access-reset conditions and delivered to the system; system recovery and protection depend on this reset control behaving correctly.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity: reset assertions are computed and registered at lines 155-156 and drive the reset output at line 161, so altered reset logic can produce an incorrect system reset. Availability: withholding or continuously asserting the reset output at line 161 can prevent the protected system from recovering or operating.",

      "Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Information": "The stored indication of whether the last recorded reset cause was debug, watchdog timeout, or access related; software depends on it to diagnose and respond to reset events.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity: the cause state is stored with distinct values at lines 169, 172, 174, and 176 and is returned in the bus response at line 111, so corruption can misreport the reset reason.",

      "Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Information": "The output control value that enables the clock-generation path used by the watchdog; watchdog operation depends on the clock remaining enabled.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity: the clock-enable output is produced from the watchdog enable setting at line 140, so changing that control changes the clock-generator command. Availability: withholding the output enable at line 140 can stop the clock required for watchdog operation.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],

  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Strict access-reset policy",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The setting only selects whether a refused or invalid access requests a reset, apart from read-back, which the reset rule excludes; it is assigned at line 96 and used only in the access-reset path at line 156."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Invalid-password or refused-write decision",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "This decision only requests a reset and records its cause under the reset rule, as shown by lines 99-106 and 156-176."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Reset password credential",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The fixed constant at line 35 has no shown storage or modification path and the comparison result is only used for reset handling at lines 102-106, so the RTL shows neither a required confidentiality mechanism nor a mutable credential asset."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command fields",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The request strobe, direction, and address only select or authorize register accesses at lines 90-92 and are excluded as access command fields rather than being information of their own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus response handshake and constant error status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The acknowledge merely copies the request strobe at line 83 and the error field is tied to a constant at line 84, so they are handshake or constant status information rather than independent assets."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset inputs",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The clock and reset inputs only time or reset internal elements at lines 73, 81, 124, 128, 151, 154, 168, and 170 and are excluded by the clocks-and-resets rule."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Prescaler tick and counter increment pulse",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "C4",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Timeout comparison flag",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "C5",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Watchdog service/reset pulse",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "C4",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus control/status read-back word",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_wdt",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The response word only carries the separately identified configuration and reset-cause values at lines 109-113, while its acknowledge and error portions are covered by handshake rules."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
